title: Lollipop Lamb Chops

yield.text: Serves 4 as a main, 8–10 as an appetizer

items.raw: 2 frenched racks of lamb (about 1½ pounds each), cut into single-bone chops
3 tablespoons olive oil, plus more for the pan
½ teaspoon freshly ground black pepper
Flaky salt and lemon wedges, to serve

steps.text: Stand each rack up and slice down between the bones into single chops. Clean any meat off the exposed bones with a paring knife so they look like handles.
Toss the chops with the garlic, rosemary, thyme, olive oil, salt, and pepper. Refrigerate 1 to 8 hours, then let sit at room temperature 20 minutes.
Heat a large cast-iron skillet over medium-high until it just starts to smoke. Add a thin film of oil.
Lay in the chops without crowding. Cook 2 to 3 minutes per side, until browned and the center reads 125–130°F for medium-rare. Stand them on their fatty edge for 30 seconds to render it.
Rest on a platter 5 minutes. Sprinkle with flaky salt.
Pass with lemon wedges and mint jelly, and let people pick them up by the bone.

notes.label: Frenching
notes.text: most butchers will french the racks for you if you ask; it saves a lot of fiddly work.

notes.label: On the grill
notes.text: grill over high heat 2 to 3 minutes per side. Wrap the bones in foil if you want them to stay clean.

notes.label: Ahead of time
notes.text: the chops can sit in the marinade all day. Cook them right before serving; they cool fast.

notes.label: Smoke alarm warning
notes.text: a hot cast-iron pan full of lamb fat smokes. Turn on the fan before you start.
